name: Enoxaparin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 40 mg SC once daily (first dose 2 hours before surgery), 7 to 10 days

usual_adult_dose.indication: DVT prophylaxis, hip or knee replacement
usual_adult_dose.dose: 30 mg SC every 12 hours, starting 12 to 24 hours after surgery

usual_adult_dose.indication: DVT prophylaxis, acutely ill medical patients
usual_adult_dose.dose: 40 mg SC once daily, 6 to 11 days
1 mg/kg SC every 12 hours, or 1.5 mg/kg SC once daily (inpatient)
1 mg/kg SC every 12 hours with aspirin

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets incl. aspirin and salicylates, NSAIDs (incl. ketorolac), dipyridamole
key_interactions.action: Stop these before starting enoxaparin when possible; if essential, monitor closely (clinical and laboratory).

common: Bleeding, anemia, thrombocytopenia, raised aminotransferases, diarrhea, nausea, ecchymosis, fever, edema, dyspnea, confusion, injection-site pain (>1%)
serious: Spinal/epidural hematoma with neuraxial anesthesia or puncture (boxed warning)
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) with or without thrombosis
Valve thrombosis in pregnant women with mechanical heart valves

contraindications: Immune-mediated HIT within the past 100 days or circulating antibodies
Hypersensitivity to enoxaparin, heparin or pork products
Hypersensitivity to benzyl alcohol (multiple-dose vials only)
monitoring: Screen for bleeding disorders before starting
Platelet count, hemoglobin and signs of bleeding
Kidney function (creatinine clearance) for dose selection
Anti-factor Xa levels: see approved kidney guidance for dialysis

pk.half_life: 4.5 hours (single SC dose) to about 7 hours (repeated dosing), anti-factor Xa
pk.half_life_eskd: Hemodialysis: elimination rate similar but AUC two-fold higher (single IV dose study; label)
pk.metabolism: Liver desulfation and/or depolymerization to less active fragments
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Active fragments about 10% of the dose; total renal (active and inactive) about 40%

sources.citation: Sanofi-Aventis U.S. LLC. (2026). Lovenox (enoxaparin sodium) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA020164, set ID 5017a927-2a24-4f27-89f9-27c805bf7d59, version effective May 28, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

draft_notes: Anti-Xa monitoring line points to the approved renal text rather than restating it; the label itself lists anti-Xa only in PK.
Severe kidney impairment (CrCl <30): AUC up 65% with repeated 40 mg (label PK).
